Some Inspiring Words from Pope Leo The Spirit opens borders, first of all, in our hear ts. He is the Gift that opens our lives to love. His presence breaks down o ur hardness of heart, our narrowness of mind, our selfishness, the fears that enchain us and the narcissism that makes us think only of o urselves. The Holy Spirit comes to challenge us, to make us confront t he possibility that our lives are shrivelling up, trapped in the vortex of individualism. Sadly, oddly enough, in a world of burgeoning “soci al” media, we risk being ever more alone. The Spirit of God allows us to find a new way of ap proaching and experiencing life. He puts us in touch with our inmost self, beneath all the masks we wear. He leads us to an encounter with the Lord by teaching us to experience the joy that is his gift. He convinces us, that only by abiding in love, will we receive the streng th to remain faithful to his word and to let it transform us. The Spirit also opens borders in our relationship with others . Jesus tells us that this Gift is the love between him and the Father that comes to dwell within us. We then become capable of opening our hearts to our brothers and sisters, overcoming our rigidity, moving beyond our fear of those who are different, and mas tering the passions that stir within. The Spirit also transforms those deeper, hidden dangers that disturb our relationships, like suspicion, prejudice or the desire to manipulate others. The Holy Spirit, on the other hand, brings to matur ity within us the fruits that enable us to cultivate good and healthy relationships: “love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfu lness, gentleness and self-control” ( Gal 5:22). In this way, the Spirit broadens the borders of our relationships and opens us to the joy of fra ternity. This is also a critical yardstick for the Church. For we are truly the Church of the Risen Lord and disciples of Pentecost if there are no borders or divisions among us; if we are able to dialogue and accept one another in the Church, and to reconcile our diversi ties; and if, as Church, we become a welcoming and hospitable place for all. POPE LEO Tree Planting To Remember Pope Francis To celebrate 10 years since The publication of Laudato Si and to honour the late Pope Francis, we will plant an Olive Tree in the grounds of St Mary’s at 12pm on Sunday afternoon after the 11 am mass on the 14th of September. The Mass will be celebrated by Bishop Donal Roche who will help us plant the tree afterwards. We will celebrate only one mass in the parish that weekend to facilitate this special even t Laudato Si has been a very influential document across the world in promoting care for our common home and a sense of responsibility towards our brothers and sisters world-wide who are being adversely affected by change. Please come along to honour and celebrate the amazing contribution that Pope Francis made in promoting “c are for our common home”. Why an Olive Tree? In the Bible, the olive tree carries significant sy mbolic meaning, representing peace, prosperity, and divine blessing. The olive branch, in particular, is a uni versal symbol of peace and reconciliation, as seen in the story of Noah and the dove. A great big thank you to Jimmy O Gorman for the research , and who will lovingly prepare the home our tree! July 26th Feast of Saints Joachim and Anne, the Patron Saints of Grandparents : The “feast of grandparents” reminds grandparents of their responsibility to establish a tone for generations to come: They must make the traditions live and offer them as a promise to little children. But the feast has a message for the younger generation as well. I t reminds the young that older people’s greater persp ective, depth of experience, and appreciation of life’s pro found are all part of a wisdom hugely beneficial to us all Generations Prayer. God, you have blessed me indeed as the child I love has had a child I love with all that is within me. I pray that you watch over and protect grandchild as you have always done for me. May their lives be long and healthy. May they have the courage to follow their dreams, and should the day come when I am no longer on Earth with them, may they look back up on me with fond memories, and may they never forget th at they were and always will be deeply loved by me. . . Thought for the Month "It is not joy that makes us grateful; it is gratit ude that makes us joyful." — David Steindl-Rast November Themes Remembrance: Honouring loved ones who have passed away, alongside historical reflecti on and remembrance days.
Gratitude: Shifting focus from grand gestures to everyday blessings, small joys, and inner peace.

Transition: Letting go of the last remnants of autumn and embracing slower, cosier indoor Renewal: Using the shorter days as an invitation to pause, take stock of the year, and reset. "The month of November makes me feel that life is passing more quickly.

In an effort to slow it down, I try to fill the hours more meaningfully." — Henry Rollins Scripture quote of the month "And hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured i nto our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us . Come and light a candle for your loved ones St. Martin de Porres.
Martin lived in 16th- and 17th-century Peru and experienced racial prejudice and poverty h imself.
He devoted his life to caring for sick people, serving the poor and treating people of different backgrounds with compassion.

He also cared for animals. What makes him especially relevant is that he lived out the equality of human dignity in a society deeply divided by race a nd class . He did not reserve his kindness for people who were socially respectable or powerful.
November Prayer "As the leaves fall and the days grow shorter, November gently slows us down.
It is a month where memory meets hope. We light candles for those we love and miss, trusting that the light of Christ shines brig hter than any darkness.
May our parish be a harbour of comfort th is month— holding space for grief, offering gratitude for lives well-lived, and walking gently together into the promise of God's peace.

What is The Living Room? The Living Room is a special ecumenical collaboration between Powerscourt Parish and St. Mary’s Parish, Enniskerry.
Our monthly gatherings offer a different and refreshing way to pray.

The Living Room has become much more than a time of prayer and reflecti on; it is a warm, welcoming space where friendships have grown, support is shared, and a real sense of community has developed . An important part of our gathering is the opportunity to enjoy a cup of tea or coffee together afterwards.
This relaxed social time allows friendships to deepen, conversations to continue and new connections to flourish in a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere.
